correctness.rationale: The eight token-pair types yield three vertex-disjoint induced blocks and only two extra edge classes. In each incidence block a cycle matching and an explicit endpoint/pair cover attain min(t,C(t,2)); the mixed block has a+b disjoint edges by Hall or an explicit singleton-branch matching, and a cover XV union UY. Their disjoint union gives equal-size matching and global vertex cover. All minima are forced to be blockwise minima; the mixed block cover is uniquely XV union UY, with separate singleton-branch forcing. The incidence block has two minimum covers only at size three. Complementation proves both formulas and exactly the independent optimizer choices. All parameter boundaries (a,b>=1) are covered, and the packaged standard-library verifier builds token edges directly from the host and checks 64 sizes and 9 exact optimizer counts.

value.rationale: The result answers a natural extremal question for the same two-token double-star family whose domination number was recently determined, adding an exact matching/independence formula and a complete maximum-configuration classification. The factor-two degeneracy localized precisely at three-leaf branches, and unique optimal configurations for all other sizes, are structural rather than mere numerical small-instance facts. The all-parameter result offers exact test cases and demonstrates how host degree transitions control optimizer rigidity. It does not assert a general token-graph theorem.
